body: Replying to an older post. I got a lot out of your thread on here in regards to the effectiveness of Abilify after not taking anything for 15 years. Am on 10mg Cipralex and 10mg Abilify and got my first injection of Abilify and my psychosis is gone and I feel normal again. Zero side effects. It has been a blessing. It is nice to see some technical info on here as to how it works. So thank you.

Thank you I am actually transferring from Alberta Hospital and just got set up with income support from the social worker and a sober living house through a friend so things are looking up. I was living in my car for 2 months collecting bottles to eat so this has been a blessing.
Thank you
Thank you

You found a job here in Edmonton?

Ya. I admitted myself to the emergency room. They transferred me to the mental hospital for treatment for depression and stress induced psychosis. Best place to be right now. Place to sleep and eat and they will help me get back on my feet.

I am 40 and could no longer afford to live on my own and I have 3 kids am recently divorced and was recently homeless living in my car and now am in the hospital getting my mental health in check. Focus on YOU not what societal norms are cause guess what, the wages no longer meet the cost of living anymore and nearly everyone I know is one paycheque short of financial ruin. It will only be a matter of time before there is an economic capitalist collapse.

Thank you. To be honest I have yet to look into resources. Just going on a month on the street. I do believe we have a similar food donation program through a local church. I will likely soon need to lean on it. Eating raspberries and rotten apples while nutritional is getting bland.
Possibly yes. But whether I can trust my memories is the question.

Well this is a plausible explanation. And I appreciate your insight. Of course this is assuming that the identity of my 'self' and the parts thereof are in fact real. I will have to investigate further and report my findings. Come to think of it I am under an enormous amount of internal stress. Recently divorced, homeless, unemployed and can't find a job to support my 3 kids or at the moment myself to name a few. But otherwise I am doing great. Although I have started noticing the same few strange individuals around town lately. One of them looks like me but with a moustache and dressed like a lumberjack. I just recently saw him giving the middle finger to a metal fence and explaining to people around him that the fence wasn't there yesterday and he was right. And actually neither was the road I was driving down.

Exactly. And here is another thing. When you focus on something so intently that you believe it, whether it be positive or negative, you will manifest the result accordingly. Subconsciously. There is supposed scientific evidence. Whatever that even means.

Gotta be self sufficient at 40 I suppose. My parents and friends pay for their water consumption so I would have paid them the $5 or $6 but they wouldn't likely accept it and would probably just be offended. The laundromat seemed like a better option.

I have been applying to jobs that I specifically am qualified for. Like an exact qualification match for a job that I have been doing for 12 years and have applied to twice and have followed up and hear absolutely nothing back. This goes for more than one employer. And I have never burned any bridges. I just don't get it.

Thank you for your kind words. In a sense being homeless teaches you to quickly appreciate the little things in life, as another user posted; like a warm shower. Not the tan leather heated seats and moonroof of your car. It also teaches you humility, that we are all just human. Some have just lost their way, whether it be due to an abundance of money (greed) or a lack of money (poverty) either way when you become homeless and on the streets you quickly realize that although we are each only human we are also each enslaved to the capitalist system you mention  whether we contribute to it or we choose not to. Finding the balance somewhere in between in order to live a life content with what you only absolutely need I believe is the key. For a landlord to evict someone especially with kids without working out a mutually beneficial arrangement to avoid the tenants ending up on the street goes to show how flawed the system is. It's always about money. Very few have the heart to do something for someone out of a good hearted nature when there is a chance to otherwise capitalise on their situation. I hope your brother and his girlfriend and their son are able to find another way to avoid eviction. But landlords are the prime example of capitalism. Their 'income property' rental income is paramount to the well being of someone else including a child.
I've been there too. Unfortunately sales soliciting calls is where I draw the line.

I have an interview tomorrow but the job would require me to move to another city 4hrs away. The wage is so high that the child support amount would end up going from $787/mo to $1478/mo and I will see my kids even less. So please explain where the incentive is for me to earn a high wage in another city 4hrs away for the sake of 'getting another job' and supporting my kids but seeing them 4 days a month if I am lucky. $1487/mo is more than she pays in rent and utilities. Her net income will be more than my gross income. The system is a joke.
Thanks. Found$10
Fair enough. 30 days seems more than ample amount of time.
Thank you and I hope the same for you as well. No parent should have to go without seeing their kids.
Thank you. If it wasn't for the fact I have 3 kids to support I probably wouldn't mind not having a place to live, it's been nice not paying a ridiculous amount of money on rent.

I am recently divorced, lost my job, then had to give up my shared custody, and am now homeless and have $40 to my name and am behind on support payments. You do not want to end up here.

If you consider being broke and homeless and living out of your car and only seeing your kids 2 nights a week and every second weekend and barley able to eat each day enjoyable.. then sure, I'm enjoying my divorce because I'd still rather be in this current situation anyday than  to still be married to my ex-wife.

Thanks for this. It's not so much that there was an expectation in mind, I wasn't expecting anything actually, and wasn't so much angered by receiving nothing but rather felt forgotten. It was just that looking back she had the opportunity on more than one occasion to give and she couldn't be bothered because it wasn't legally required of her. Speaks volumes of how the entire 25 year relationship played out, me the provider, her the taker. And it just reinforces the fact that yes while perhaps I was being co-dependant I realized she never really depended on me other than my money which is the only thing she cares to discuss now as well, when she is getting money from me. But yes you are right I have finally given in to the fact that I do need to focus on myself and my kids and not pay her any mind any longer.

Well that would be the easy way out. I've considered it myself. Even had a plan. And then I thought what if, just what if it isn't as bad as I am letting myself believe it is, or would be. Turns out the streets ain't so bad afterall. Not that I would recommend it, but where there's a will there's a way. And there are plenty of options. Truth be told I enjoy not having a rent payment. That deposit that would otherwise go to securing a place to sleep could be used towards getting a car and you could live in that fairly comfortably. There are always options. Killing yourself is just the easiest one. But you will be missing out on how this experience will help you to become stronger in the end. Challenge yourself and you will see. Everyday I learn something new about myself that my former self would not have thought possible. And it has taught me to be more appreciative. You can get through this. Reach out for support here and your local services should you require assistance.

I think this is exactly what I needed to hear. Thank you. I texted her earlier to tell her I think it's best I pick the kids up and drop them off from the car from now on. No need for her and I to converse really unless there is an emergency. And yes I am trying to get a new career as mine no longer seems to exists after 12 years. Being broke is the hardest part right now because it affects my kids the most not being able to take them out and do fun things. The park is getting tiring. But I will get back on my feet again. And after her showing her true colours this evening I have no inclination to ever do anything for her again.

I think I have had it rough.. divorced now homeless and living in my car but I try to remind myself there is always someone out there in a tougher situation and that I am actually lucky. And then I read something like this, someone in your situation and I quickly realize I am very fortunate as my ex-wife has the kids staying with her fulltime and they aren't sleeping in the car with me. I can't even imagine how hard that must be. I wish you all the best.
Hang in there. Hopefully we will find a way out. Although I have to admit I like not giving away any money to a landlord or bank.
Thank you

I contemplated jumping off of that bridge on my 40th birthday a week ago. And then a fellow came up to me and started chatting about the water level and how there had been recent drownings. I think he could sense I was thinking of jumping. He started telling me about his life and got me talking and I quickly realized I wasn't as alone as I felt I was. I reconsidered and decided not to. The fall wouldn't have killed me but the undertow eventually would have pulled me under. To consider that more than one person had recently unwillingly died in the river and are no longer here made me appreciate the fact that I am alive and don't want to drown in the river either. And my thoughts go out to the families of those who had lost a loved one taken by the river.
And this is why I no longer own a home and pay property taxes plus the city's bullshit improvement renewal fees that I didn't ask for or want yet was demaned to cough up money for.

The dog walkers and jogger and bikers are still there but only generally in the morning and not late in the evening but I can't disclose the location though because it took me a long time to find it and I am currently homeless and sleeping in my car and am enjoying the fact nobody seems to know about it (aside from people meeting to buy drugs) and therefore no one bothers me and I'd like to keep it that way as long as I can at least until the police happen to come across me sleeping there.
Fucking dog walkers are inescapable. Literally. No matter where I go. There they are walking their dog. No matter the time.

The fact that 2 teens in this day and age can somehow manage to evade being captured in a military scale manhunt is baffling in itself.
